title: Availability snapshot
description: What the local account can run right now, per harness — and, on disk, the cache file the host names (src/host.ts routingPaths cacheFile), mode 0600. Every object here is closed: an implementation cannot quietly add a token, an email or an open account id, because a document carrying one stops validating. Version 2 (ADR-004) adds the harness tier, the window kind and scope, and the hidden mark on a model; a version 1 document is discarded rather than migrated.

fingerprint.description: Opaque local key, present only when accounts must be told apart. Hex, and one-way: the original identifier must not be recoverable from it.

harnesses.description: One entry per harness probed. A harness the workspace does not declare is absent, not 'unavailable'.

state.description: available — auth, model and limit confirmed; exhausted — the limit is confirmably spent; unavailable — no binary, no auth, no model, or the harness is broken; unknown — the state could not be established.

reason.description: Stable reason code. The list is fixed in ADR-003, unchanged by ADR-004, and written once in docs/reference/03-cli.md.
null exactly when the state is available and nothing qualifies it.

message.description: Human-readable diagnosis. Never the harness output verbatim: that is where a token would arrive.

source.description: probe — this run asked the harness; cache — a live entry was reused; manual — a person marked it.

resetAt.description: When an exhausted limit is known to reset. null means unknown, and an exhaustion with no reset is cleared only by --clear-exhausted.

version.description: Harness binary version, when the probe read it.

tier.description: The plan this account is on (ADR-004). null when the harness names none. Carried and displayed; an input to no score in v1.

credits.description: Whether the account holds spendable credits beside its windows. Informational: nothing scores it and nothing spends one.

resetCredits.description: How many window resets the account may spend. Informational, and surfaced rather than used: spending one is a person's decision.

models.description: Model inventory this account exposes. A model the catalog does not rate is carried with rated:false and is shown but never chosen automatically.

windows.description: Normalised subscription windows. Absent when the harness exposes none; the resolver then treats remaining as unknown.

tier.description: ADR-004: the plan name and where it came from. A tier is a property of the PLAN, shared by everyone on it — which is why it does not break the cache's promise to hold no identity, and why the derived form carries the plan's included amount and never the account's used amount.

name.description: Shaped like a code, not like prose: no spaces and no '@', so this field cannot become a second route for harness output or for an address.

source.description: credentials — a local credential record, read with no request; probe — the harness answered; derived — computed where no method names the plan; user — the person answered the question once, in the user overlay.

rated.description: Whether the merged catalog carries a tuple for this model.

hidden.description: The harness lists this row and declines to offer it (ADR-004). Carried so a person sees the whole inventory; the resolver's inventory is the rows without it, so a tuple naming one is excluded as model-not-in-inventory.

flags.description: Marks the harness prints next to the model. Carried, not judged: a policy that cares denies the flag or the model in an overlay. The list is CLOSED (ADR-004), because an overlay may select by a flag and a name checked against nothing would let a person's typo ban silently nothing — the cost is that a new mark a harness starts printing needs a release rather than a data change.

window.description: One limit period of the account. ADR-004 makes kind and lengthSec required and scope explicit: kind is a NAME and lengthSec is the number, and neither is derived from the other — a billing cycle is monthly and is not thirty days. An adapter that cannot state a length reports no window at all.

scope.description: What the window binds. null — the whole account. A scope that covers models names them BY ID, so the resolver matches exactly and infers no family.

modelScope.description: One model family, as the harness named it. `model` is the harness's own display name; `models` is that name resolved to catalog-comparable ids by the adapter holding the driver's dictionary. A display name the adapter cannot resolve arrives WITHOUT `models`: the window stays in the snapshot, is printed for a person, and binds nothing.

autoPoolScope.description: The pool whose model list the harness publishes. `models` is required here: the list is a fact the harness stated, and a pool that covers named models without naming them binds nothing.

apiPoolScope.description: The complement pool: every model in no auto list falls here. It carries NO `models`, because a list of everything else is not a fact any harness stated.

example-pooled.message: authenticated; one cycle with two pools

example-quiet.message: authenticated, but this harness exposes no limit source
